concept: Ollama runner no-mmap default on Metal and use_mmap option
summary: 2024-06: maintainer advised {"options": {"use_mmap": false}} to cure thrashing (issue 3940).

facts.text: 2024-06: maintainer advised {"options": {"use_mmap": false}} to cure thrashing (issue 3940).
2024-09: PR 6854 proposed OLLAMA_NO_MMAP to force --no-mmap globally; no maintainer merge is visible on the page.
2025-01 and 2025-04 logs show --no-mmap on Metal and Linux partial offload (issues 8571, 10104, 7081).
By v0.12.0 the loader is split into an Ollama engine (no mmap) and a llama engine (mmap rules above).

Layer count: the Metal rule triggers on NumGPU between 1 and block_count, so a model Ollama decides to split (for example 9 of 62 layers) always loads with no mmap, which cannot load a model larger than RAM.
Forcing mmap on is only possible per request or Modelfile (use_mmap true), not with an environment variable.
Disabling mmap crashed some models in a 2024 report even with fewer layers (issue 3940).

Reporters in issue 4895 say --no-mmap is slightly faster and avoids RAM spikes on 8 GB machines; the Ollama staff reply in PR 6854 asks whether mmap should instead be disabled by default. Not resolved on the page.
Whether PR 6854 was merged (page shows no merged marker; "Closed" appears twice, which I read as closed unmerged but did not verify).
Behavior in releases after v0.12.0; the main-branch llm/server.go fetched here is a 289-line stub with no mmap logic.
Ollama's code comment reads "mmap has issues with partial offloading on metal" and sets UseMMap to false when a metal GPU has 0 < NumGPU < BlockCount + 1.
In v0.6.2, --no-mmap is appended when (Windows, CUDA, UseMMap nil) or (Linux, free memory < estimated total, UseMMap nil) or (CPU library, UseMMap nil) or UseMMap explicitly false.
The same rules appear in v0.12.0 as loadRequest.UseMmap = false, and v0.12.0 notes "Mmap is only supported on the llama engine"; the Ollama engine path leaves the legacy UseMmap field unused.
Ollama's Options struct has UseMMap *bool with JSON name use_mmap, and the default options set UseMMap to nil.
A Metal log (Ollama.app, 2025-01-24) offloading 9 of 62 layers of a 413.6 GiB model on a 48 GiB machine shows --n-gpu-layers 9 --no-mmap.
A Linux log (Ollama 0.6.2, 2025-04-03) shows --n-gpu-layers 21 --no-mmap and "load_tensors ... (mmap = false)" for a 250 GB model.
A maintainer's workaround for forcing mmap is the client option {"use_mmap": true}; ollama serve --help and ollama run --help expose no mmap flag.

A 2024-06 maintainer reply tells a user whose model thrashed to send options {"use_mmap": false}, and the user reported it "works nicely"; a second user saw crashes with mmap disabled unless num_gpu was also reduced.

PR 6854 proposed OLLAMA_NO_MMAP=1 to always add --no-mmap to the llama runner; a reviewer asked what problem mmap caused and whether it should be off by default, and commenters later asked for updates and for a way to force mmap on.

Issue 4895 requested a global use_mmap environment variable because many front ends cannot set it; the reporter claims --no-mmap costs 5-10 s more load time on an 8 GB RAM, 6 GB VRAM PC but avoids RAM at 99 percent.
Issue 10539 (2025-05-02, Ollama 0.6.7, closed) asked for a global use_mmap variable after reporting that with use_mmap true, model RAM was not fully released after unload and load times were worse.

On a Mac, a model that fits fully on the GPU loads with mmap by default under the llama engine, so its weights are reclaimable file cache until Metal touches them; a split model loads into anonymous memory.
